course_description:
This course explores the challenges that convicted offenders face through processes of rehabilitation, reentry, and reintegration. Through an exploration of a range of corrections topics, students will gain knowledge about current and past correctional management practices. Students will be exposed to evidence-based concepts, research and policy from experts in the field. Students will gain critical knowledge and skills that will help them to contribute as practitioners in the field.

Given dramatically rising imprisonment rates in Australia and other countries, it is necessary to increase our understanding of correctional practices and their contribution to the rehabilitation and re-entry of prisoners. This course enables students to explore evidence and research on correctional systems, rehabilitation practices and effective offender risk assessment, treatment, re-entry, and reintegration. The course examines research, policy and practice across different correctional domains and examines data on offending risks and rehabilitation programs. The course gives students the opportunity to learn about and apply skills and concepts necessary to work in a correctional practice setting.

The course involves weekly seminar activities that will help you to develop knowledge and skills in relation to correctional practice. The topics of the seminars vary and will include interaction with field practitioners who are expert in areas of offender risk assessment, rehabilitation and community-based corrections.

The course relies heavily on Blackboard in order to provide students with learning materials and activities relevant to each week’s learning module. Students are strongly encouraged to familiarise themselves with the course Blackboard site before the first week.ﾠ

Students are expected to spend at least 8 hours each week on this course . This time can be divided roughly into three contact hours, which comprise a combination of seminar discussion, recorded and/or live lectures, and Industry Partner presentations. The remaining five non-contact hours should be spent carefully reading and critically reflecting upon the required readings, as well as reviewing previous class materials and completing the assessment tasks.

course_aims: The aim of this course is to provide students with the ability to critically reflect on the current theoretical and evidence-based processes and practices of correctional work. Correctional practice and policy related to rehabilitation have changed in ways that affect both offenders and workforces. The intention of this course is to provide knowledge and critical-thinking and practical skills for students interested in the diverse and dynamic fields related to offender re-entry and corrections more broadly.ﾠ

learning_outcomes.description: Understand core theories, principles, and practices of offender rehabilitation, re-entry and reintegration;
Demonstrate enhanced skills of critical thinking and reflection in diverse contexts;
Demonstrate enhanced communication employable in diverse settings; and
Demonstrate capacity to review, evaluate and apply evidence for achieving best practice outcomes.

assessment_details.task_description: Throughout the semester, a series of guest speakers from organisations such as Queensland Corrective Services and Victoria Police will present in lectures. These presentations provide important insights into contemporary correctional practice and offender rehabilitation. Students are expected to attend these sessions and select one (1) guest speaker presentation to analyse. You can choose any guest speaker. You are required to produce a concise, critical summary and reflection (maximum 3 pages) addressing the questions outlined below. Your response should be structured into the following sections: Section 1: Understanding the Presentation Provide a clear and accurate summary of the presentation by addressing the following: · Who was the guest speaker (e.g., role, professional background, organisation)? · What is the main focus of their work? · Identify and briefly explain 2–3 key points emphasised by the speaker. · What types of evidence, case studies, or professional experiences did the speaker draw upon? Section 2: Critical Analysis Demonstrate critical engagement with the presentation: · What do you interpret as the speaker’s overall message regarding corrections and offender rehabilitation? · What were the strongest aspects of the speaker’s arguments or insights? Explain why they were effective or persuasive. Section 3: Reflection Reflect on your learning and perspective: · What is one key insight you gained from this presentation? · Did the presentation challenge or reinforce your views on corrections or offender rehabilitation? Explain your response with reference to specific points from the presentation. Assessment Requirements: Length: Maximum of 3 pages. Formatting: 1.5 spacing; 12 p font. Structure: Use clear headings and subheadings corresponding to each section Referencing: Not required, unless you draw on course materials (in which case, use appropriate academic referencing). Due Date: Submit any time by Week 11 Attendance is a requirement for this assessment. Students who do not attend the guest speaker presentation will receive 0 marks for their submission (e.g. if you submit the summary and reflection but you did not attend that guest speaker’s presentation, this will result in a zero mark for this submission). It is the student's responsibility to ensure that their attendance is recorded. Marking criteria: Criteria including rubrics are available in the ‘Assessments’ folder on the course Blackboard site. assessment_details.title: Case and risk formulation report
assessment_details.task_description: Students are required to complete a case and risk formulation based on an assigned offender profile, using the HCR-20 V3 risk assessment framework. For this assessment, you will: Apply the HCR-20 V3 framework to analyse the offender profile Develop a structured case formulation integrating relevant risk factors Arrive at a final risk judgement regarding the offender’s likelihood of future violent offending. Propose scenario planning and risk management strategies to mitigate or reduce the risk of reoffending, particularly in the context of potential parole Assessment Requirements: Maximum length: 1,500 words (excluding references). Format: 1.5 spaced, 12 point font. Structure: Use clear headings and subheadings to organise key sections. Referencing: Include a reference list at the end of the report. Students must select ONE of two offender profiles, which will be made available on the course learning site. This assessment requires you to apply a structured professional risk assessment tool to a hypothetical case. It is designed to reflect work-integrated learning, simulating real-world practice in offender risk assessment and management. Relevant materials and guidance for completing this task are available on the course learning site. To assist students with this assessment, Week 12 will be dedicated to reviewing the assessment requirements, covering examples of case and risk formulations, and providing students with the opportunity to discuss their plans or drafts in consultation with the course coordinator.
